intro: Widening a hidden layer changes both adjacent weight matrices. Account for each layer before allocating a network.
task: Return per-layer weight, bias, and total counts, plus the total network parameter count.
requirements: widths is an integer vector of length 2..64, with entries 1..64. biases contains one numeric 0/1 flag per consecutive pair of widths.
Return {"weights": vector, "biases": vector, "per_layer": vector, "total": scalar}. A layer from a inputs to b outputs has a*b weights and b biases when enabled.

Use finite real numeric values of magnitude at most 1e6, excluding boolean inputs. Each array axis has 1..64 entries and at most 65536 elements total unless a stricter bound is stated. Return NumPy arrays for array outputs, preserve caller inputs, and raise ValueError for invalid inputs.

examples.name: Two layers
examples.output:
{'weights': [12, 8], 'biases': [4, 2], 'per_layer': [16, 10], 'total': 26}
(NumPy arrays shown as lists; rounded to 12 significant digits.)

examples.name: No bias
examples.output:
{'weights': [6], 'biases': [0], 'per_layer': [6], 'total': 6}
(NumPy arrays shown as lists; rounded to 12 significant digits.)

examples.name: Mixed flags
examples.output:
{'weights': [2, 2], 'biases': [0, 1], 'per_layer': [2, 3], 'total': 5}
(NumPy arrays shown as lists; rounded to 12 significant digits.)

hints.title: Follow the data
hints.body: Adjacent widths describe a parameter block; the input layer has none.

hints.title: Check the boundary
hints.body: Disabling bias removes one parameter per output neuron.

explanation: Each dense output neuron connects to every input coordinate. Counting adjacent pairs exposes why changing one hidden width affects two parameter blocks.
Parameter storage differs from activation storage and dataset size. Bias flags change the trainable count without changing the number of output neurons.
